title: Firecrawl + Docker Sandboxes: Live Web Data for Sandboxed Agents
summary: Firecrawl is a launch partner for Docker Sandboxes kits. The Firecrawl kit is on Docker Kits v3 and gives any sandboxed coding agent live web search, scrape, and crawl through one allowed host, with your API key kept out of the sandbox. Available in Early Access.
body_markdown:
[Firecrawl](https://www.firecrawl.dev/) turns any website into clean, LLM-ready data. **Docker Sandboxes** run coding agents like Claude Code and Codex inside an isolated VM, where the sandbox decides which hosts the agent can reach and credentials never leave the host. **Together, you get an agent that can search, scrape, and crawl the live web without the sandbox opening up to the rest of the internet.**


Firecrawl is a launch partner for Docker Sandboxes kits, and the Firecrawl kit is now on Kits v3, with an[official guide on Docker's docs](https://docs.docker.com/guides/firecrawl-sandbox-kit/?utm_source=firecrawl&utm_medium=blog&utm_campaign=docker-sandboxes-kit) and a[walkthrough on the Docker blog](https://www.docker.com/blog/docker-sandboxes-firecrawl-web-access/?utm_source=firecrawl&utm_medium=blog&utm_campaign=docker-sandboxes-kit) . The kit adds live web access to any sandboxed agent through one allowed host, and your API key never enters the sandbox. It is available now on[Docker Hub](https://hub.docker.com/r/firecrawl/sbx-kit-firecrawl?utm_source=firecrawl&utm_medium=blog&utm_campaign=docker-sandboxes-kit) .


\[ Firecrawl kit for Docker Sandboxes \]


Give any Docker Sandbox agent


live web access


. One allowed host, and your API key stays out of the sandbox.


[Get the kit on Docker Hub](https://hub.docker.com/r/firecrawl/sbx-kit-firecrawl?utm_source=firecrawl&utm_medium=blog&utm_campaign=docker-sandboxes-kit)


Kits are in Early Access, so the steps below are current for November 2026, and the[repo README](https://github.com/firecrawl/firecrawl-docker-sandbox#readme) has the latest.


## Live web data, inside the sandbox


A sandbox with no network is safe, and it leaves the agent unable to open a docs page, check a changelog, or look up an API that shipped after its training cutoff, so the agent answers from memory and gets current APIs wrong. The usual fix is to widen network access until the agent can fetch whatever it wants, which gives back most of what the sandbox took away.


Docker's kits fix this by declaring what a sandbox adds: tools to install, domains to allow, credentials to inject, and instructions for the agent. Docker introduced Kits v3 at the WeAreDevelopers keynote in San Jose on September 24.


In v3, a kit is a plain OCI image built with` docker build` , its declarations live in the image manifest, and Docker is proposing it as an open format. The Firecrawl kit ships as a v3 mixin, published as` docker.io/firecrawl/sbx-kit-firecrawl` , and passes Docker's kit conformance suite.


The Firecrawl kit is a mixin, so it layers onto the workload and agent you already run. With it in place, your sandboxed agent can:


- [Scrape websites](https://www.firecrawl.dev/scrape) - Extract content from any webpage as clean markdown
- [Search the web](https://www.firecrawl.dev/search) - Run a search and get page content back with the results
- [Crawl websites](https://www.firecrawl.dev/crawl) - Gather content across a site or a docs section
- [Reach Alexandria](https://www.firecrawl.dev/alexandria) - Query Firecrawl's structured third-party data layer on API keys enabled for the[beta](https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/introducing-alexandria-series-b)


All of it goes through one added host,` api.firecrawl.dev` . The kit adds to the sandbox's allowlist and does not narrow it, so what else the agent can reach is set by your global` sbx` policy. Docker's` balanced` preset allows package registries, GitHub, and a curated list of vendor domains, and returns a 403 for general websites, including most documentation sites. Firecrawl is the agent's route to those.


## How it works


The kit does four things when a sandbox starts:


1. **Installs the[Firecrawl Python SDK](https://docs.firecrawl.dev/sdks/python)** at a pinned version, and fails sandbox creation if the install or the import check fails.
2. **Declares a` firecrawl` credential.** Your API key lives in the` sbx` secret store on the host. Inside the sandbox the agent sees a placeholder, and the proxy swaps in the real key on requests to` api.firecrawl.dev` .
3. **Allows outbound traffic to` api.firecrawl.dev`** at runtime, and PyPI only during install.
4. **Gives the agent instructions** so it knows the capability exists, how to call it, and which limits come from the sandbox rather than from Firecrawl.


You need the` sbx` CLI, version 0.46 or later (on macOS,` brew trust docker/tap && brew install docker/tap/sbx` , then` sbx login` and, once,` sbx policy init balanced` ), and a Firecrawl API key from[firecrawl.dev/app/api-keys](https://www.firecrawl.dev/app/api-keys) . In this walkthrough, Claude Code reads a library changelog. Under the` balanced` policy the sandbox proxy blocks documentation sites with a 403, so the agent has to go through Firecrawl.


**1. Store the key once on the host.** The kit holds no key, and` sbx run` takes no` -e` flag for it. Run the command with no input and it prompts for the key; paste the` fc-...` value from your Firecrawl dashboard. If the key is already in an environment variable, pipe it in instead with` echo "$FIRECRAWL_API_KEY" | sbx secret set firecrawl` . Service secrets apply to every sandbox by default.


```text
sbx   secret   set   firecrawl
sbx   secret   ls
```


The kit's credential is required, so in v3` sbx` refuses to create the sandbox until the key is stored.


**2. Start a sandbox with the kit.** v3 mixins compose onto a v3 workload. This command starts Docker's shell workload, adds the Claude Code mixin, and adds the Firecrawl mixin. The trailing` .` mounts your project directory, so run it from the project, since` sbx` refuses to mount your home folder.


```text
sbx   run   docker.io/docker/sbx-kit-shell:1.0.0   --name   firecrawl-claude   \
--kit   docker.io/docker/sbx-kit-claude-mixin:2.1.285   \
--kit   docker.io/firecrawl/sbx-kit-firecrawl:1.0.0   .
```


On the first run,` sbx` asks you to approve sending the` firecrawl` credential to` api.firecrawl.dev` . Accept the defaults, since the value already lives in the secret store. Claude Code can use an Anthropic key stored with` sbx secret set anthropic` , or you can sign in when it first starts. v3 kits are versioned images, so you reference them by tag.


**3. Check that the pieces are in place.** The shell workload opens a shell inside the sandbox. This scrapes a page through the API and exercises the SDK, the credential, and the network rule in one call:


```text
python3   -   <<  'PY'
from firecrawl import Firecrawl
fc = Firecrawl()
doc = fc.scrape("https://docs.pydantic.dev/latest/changelog/", formats=["markdown"])
print(doc.markdown[:300])
PY
```


You should see the page as markdown, with its` # Changelog` heading and the latest version near the top. The same URL returns a 403 to` curl` from inside the sandbox. To confirm the key never entered the sandbox:


```text
echo   "$FIRECRAWL_API_KEY"
```


The value is the literal` proxy-managed` , the placeholder the SDK sends and the proxy replaces.


**4. Give the agent a task.** Start Claude Code with` claude` in the same shell, then ask:


```text
Use the Firecrawl Python SDK to read https://docs.pydantic.dev/latest/changelog/ and list what changed in the latest Pydantic release. Quote the page, don't answer from memory.
```


The agent scrapes the page through Firecrawl and answers from the live changelog rather than from its training data.


To build the kit from source instead of pulling it from Docker Hub, clone the repo and point` --kit` at its` firecrawl/` directory. The[README](https://github.com/firecrawl/firecrawl-docker-sandbox#2b-launch-with-a-kit-v3-workload) covers this and the v2 form of the kit for the built-in` sbx run claude` shortcut.


## What you can build with Firecrawl + Docker Sandboxes


**Coding agents that read current docs.** The agent scrapes the docs page for the library version you are on and writes code against that, instead of the version it remembers from training.


**Safe dependency upgrades.** Before an upgrade, the agent crawls the release notes and lists the breaking changes.


**Research agents in locked-down environments.** Teams with managed sandbox policy can allow one host and give every agent web search, rather than approving domains one at a time.


**Parallel agents on one key.** Store the key once, and every sandbox on the machine can use it, while the proxy keeps the value out of each one.


## Good to know


A few limits come from the sandbox, and they look like Firecrawl errors when you first hit them:


- **The kit adds one host; it does not open the web.** Under the` balanced` policy, general websites return a proxy 403 to` curl` , so a URL the agent finds in a scrape result has to be scraped through Firecrawl too. Firecrawl fetches pages on its servers, so the sandbox never needs direct access to them. Under a` deny-all` policy,` api.firecrawl.dev` is the only web host.
- **Screenshot and media formats return links on Firecrawl's storage host,** which is outside the kit's network rules, so the file cannot be downloaded from inside the sandbox.
- **Organization governance controls which domains can be allowed.** Under it, kit allow rules are inactive, so the org needs to allow` api.firecrawl.dev` . The[Docker guide](https://docs.docker.com/guides/firecrawl-sandbox-kit/?utm_source=firecrawl&utm_medium=blog&utm_campaign=docker-sandboxes-kit#how-the-kit-interacts-with-network-policy) explains how policy and the kit interact.
- **Detached and CI runs cannot answer the credential prompt.** Approve the` firecrawl` binding in one interactive run first, or write it to` ~/.config/sbx/credentials.yaml` . The[README](https://github.com/firecrawl/firecrawl-docker-sandbox#1-store-the-firecrawl-api-key) has the snippet.
- **A 402 on a scrape means the account is out of credits.** The agent is told to stop rather than retry.


## Get started


1. Install the` sbx` CLI, sign in with` sbx login` , run` sbx policy init balanced` once, and get a Firecrawl API key at[firecrawl.dev/app/api-keys](https://www.firecrawl.dev/app/api-keys)
2. Store the key with` sbx secret set firecrawl`
3. Add the kit to a v3 workload with` --kit docker.io/firecrawl/sbx-kit-firecrawl:1.0.0` , as in the[Docker guide](https://docs.docker.com/guides/firecrawl-sandbox-kit/?utm_source=firecrawl&utm_medium=blog&utm_campaign=docker-sandboxes-kit)


Issues and feature requests for the kit go to the[GitHub repo](https://github.com/firecrawl/firecrawl-docker-sandbox/issues) . Feedback on the kit format itself belongs with Docker in[docker/sandbox-kit-spec](https://github.com/docker/sandbox-kit-spec) .


---


**Ready to give your sandboxed agents live web data?**


Get the kit on[Docker Hub](https://hub.docker.com/r/firecrawl/sbx-kit-firecrawl?utm_source=firecrawl&utm_medium=blog&utm_campaign=docker-sandboxes-kit) , follow the[Firecrawl guide on Docker's docs](https://docs.docker.com/guides/firecrawl-sandbox-kit/?utm_source=firecrawl&utm_medium=blog&utm_campaign=docker-sandboxes-kit) , or get your free API key at[firecrawl.dev](https://firecrawl.dev/) .
